ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows rectangle ABCD with D at the lower left, A at the upper left, C at the lower right, and B at the upper right. Point P lies on the top side AB between A and B. Segments DP and DB are drawn from D to P and B, respectively, with DP steeper than DB. Use coordinates as assigned: set D=(0,0) and A=(0,1), so AD=1 and the top side AB has equation y=1. Since angle ADC is a right angle, and DB and DP trisect it, the three equal parts are 30 degrees each. From the image/order of rays, DB is the ray 30 degrees above DC, and DP is the ray 60 degrees above DC. For B: the ray from D at 30 degrees meets y=1. Its slope is tan 30 = 1/sqrt(3), so 1 = x_B/sqrt(3), hence x_B = sqrt(3). Thus DB = 1/sin 30 = 2. For P: the ray from D at 60 degrees meets y=1. Its slope is tan 60 = sqrt(3), so 1 = sqrt(3)x_P, hence x_P = 1/sqrt(3). Thus DP = 1/sin 60 = 2/sqrt(3). Since B and P both lie on y=1, BP = x_B - x_P = sqrt(3) - 1/sqrt(3) = 2/sqrt(3). Therefore the perimeter of triangle BDP is DB + DP + BP = 2 + 2/sqrt(3) + 2/sqrt(3) = 2 + 4/sqrt(3) = 2 + 4sqrt(3)/3.

method.method_draft: Use special right triangles plus an isosceles triangle observation. From the image, note AB is horizontal and parallel to DC, and P and B both lie on AB. From the text, DB and DP trisect the 90-degree angle ADC, so ∠CD B=30 degrees, ∠BDP=30 degrees, and ∠PDA=30 degrees. In right triangle DCB, BC=AD=1 and ∠CDB=30 degrees, so it is a 30-60-90 triangle with hypotenuse DB=2. Since AB is parallel to DC, the angle between DB and BP is also 30 degrees, so in triangle BDP we have ∠BDP=30 degrees and ∠DBP=30 degrees. Therefore DP=BP. The remaining angle ∠DPB is 120 degrees. If DP=BP=x, then by the Law of Cosines on base DB, 2^2=x^2+x^2-2x^2 cos 120=3x^2, so x=2/√3. Thus the perimeter is DB+DP+BP=2+2/√3+2/√3=2+4√3/3.
